body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), the explicit local-polynomial learners satisfy \(\mathsf G_n\). In particular, \(\mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n)\) and therefore \(n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n=O_P\{n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\}=o_P(1)\) because \(\beta>5/12\); bounded foldwise empirical increments give \(\sqrt{\log n}\,\mathfrak R_n=o_P(1)\); and the smooth plug-in estimates give \((\log n)\mathfrak K_n=o_P(1)\) and \(|\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)-1|=o_P(1)\). More generally, whenever \(\mathsf G_n\) holds and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), optimized-value stability gives \(\{S_n-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))=o_P(1)\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\).
body.justification: This separates the actual product, local empirical, variance-normalization, and clock thresholds required at the moving Gumbel level from the stronger instrumental assumptions used to verify them.
body.gap: Published pointwise causal-isotonic LR theory requires a nuisance product small relative to one cube-root neighborhood; the displayed conditions add the logarithmic accuracy needed after scanning order \(n^{1/3}\) dependent neighborhoods.
body.consumer: Three remainder clauses are algebraically supported; the centered V-statistic term and optimized-value stability remain prerequisites for implementation.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform fold-conditional maximal inequality for the fitted validation-fold V-statistic and a proof that the four numerical transfer remainders imply stability of both optimized isotonic objectives remain missing.
obligation.obstruction: The validation-fold marginalization is a dependent V-statistic. In addition, optimized-value comparison needs common contact localization and slope envelopes, but neither property is a clause of the frozen transfer condition.
obligation.attempted: The product-bias, variance plug-in, and spatial-clock plug-in rates were derived; a Hoeffding decomposition gives the required polynomial scale for a fixed bounded marginalization kernel; and a deterministic optimized-value inequality reduces the remaining comparison to contact localization and slope control.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on the zeroth-order rates calculated in the preceding partial result, the definition of \(\mathfrak B_n\) gives
\[
 \mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n).
\]
Therefore
\[
 n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n
 =O_P\!\left(n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\right)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \frac56-2\beta=-\frac16+\frac{d+1}{2s}<0,
\]
where the strict inequality follows from \(s>3(d+1)\).  Stable product, quotient, and integration inequalities, together with \(\texttt{ass:variance}\), similarly imply
\[
 \mathfrak K_n=O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right)
\]
and
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathcal V}_n}{\mathcal V(P)}-1\right|
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}
              +n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right)=o_P(1).
\]
For the pure validation-fold marginalization term, let one fold have size \(N\asymp n\), let \(I\) have length \(h\), and let \(\phi\) be bounded and continuously differentiable.  The off-diagonal part of
\[
 \frac1{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N
 \mathbf 1\{A_i\in I\}
 \left[\phi(A_i,W_j)-\int\phi(A_i,w)p(w)\,dw\right]
\]
has a zero first-coordinate projection, a second-coordinate projection of order \(h\), and a degenerate kernel with second moment of order \(h\).  Independence in \(\texttt{ass:iid}\) and the upper design-density bounds consequently give
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{h}{\sqrt n}+\frac{\sqrt h}{n}+\frac1n\right).
\]
At \(h=H_n=n^{-1/3}(\log n)^2\), multiplication by \(n^{2/3}\sqrt{\log n}\) sends each of these three terms to zero.

There is also a deterministic optimized-value inequality.  On a fixed interval, suppose both relevant monotone classes consist of functions bounded in absolute value by \(M_0\), and define
\[
 L_X(v)=\int v^2\,dt-2\int v\,dX.
\]
If \(\|X-\widetilde X\|_\infty\le\eta\), integration by parts and \(\operatorname{TV}(v)\le2M_0\) show
\[
 |L_X(v)-L_{\widetilde X}(v)|
 \le 8M_0\eta.
\]
Taking the infimum over the unconstrained class and the constrained subclass separately yields an LR optimized-value difference at most \(16M_0\eta\).  Thus the remaining transfer step is precisely to prove, uniformly at the moving level, common contact localization and a common slope envelope \(M_0\), and to prove the fitted-kernel version of the displayed uniform interval bound.  None of those properties is one of the four scalar clauses defining \(\mathsf G_n\).
